findings.summary: When the serving app carries no harness auth (`harness_auth` absent, or an empty `HarnessAuthState`), `resolve_mcp_run_agent_identity` trusts the client-asserted tenant_id/user_id (fail-open identity). The P7 tests pin this (test_acc_12_local_dev_state_without_credentials_trusts_client_assertion, test_acc_03_..._lab_identity_uses_definition_defaults) but neither the package nor R-P7-06 states it, and no L3 test exercises an unauthenticated host. MCP-ACC-10/11/12 `COVERED` therefore holds only for hosts with a configured credential.
evidence: intergrax/applications/_shared/mcp_harness_principal.py lines 92-153 (fall-through to asserted/default tenant when auth is None or local-dev)
findings.impact: A host that mounts MCP without harness auth accepts any tenant/user from the client. This is existing, tested behaviour and not a regression, but it is an unrecorded residual of the exposure engine.
findings.disposition_suggestion: Add a residual (R-P8-01) to the package and the matrix stating the behaviour and its precondition; the product question (fail closed at composition) is an operator decision and a product change would trigger ACT-N11, so it is out of the findings-only correction loop unless the operator rules otherwise.

findings.summary: R-P7-02 is disclosed honestly and the exclusion from the regression selection is justified for P7 scope, but the claim `same set` is not reproduced exactly and the cause is not established. Own reproduction of the three files: 13 failed / 16 passed at the freeze SHA, 12 failed / 17 passed at c59892829; the package and baseline logs say 11 / 11. The core 11 reproduce (LLMProviderNotConfiguredError, StrictAgentContractAuthorityError, TL11 subprocess startup timeout); the extra 1-2 (test_tl11_e2e_slow_list_within_deadline, test_tl11_e2e_http_ingress_rejects_missing_api_key) are further TL11 subprocess startup timeouts, i.e. the failing set varies from run to run. The files are marked `gate` (test_mcp_surface_opt_in_runtime.py is `no_ci`); pull_request and push CI run only the smoke profile and the full gate is manual, so green CI on PR #474 says nothing about them. One file guards the MCP opt-in default (test_scaffold_defaults_mcp_to_opt_in) and is cited as existing evidence in the implementation inventory.
evidence: .github/workflows/unit-tests.yml (profiles: PR/push smoke; full gate workflow_dispatch only)
git log: 6d436f323 `fix(llm): require explicit provider selection` (product hardening; tests last touched 5b193842e 2026-09-12 and 23640a6e7 2026-10-25)
findings.impact: Not a blocker for the P7 claims (no MCP-ACC row depends on these files and they are not counted as passing). It is an open limitation: an MCP opt-in guard and the TL11 physical catalog E2E are red or non-deterministic on this machine and unproven in CI.
findings.disposition_suggestion: Keep R-P7-02 open as a stated limitation of the closure (not a blocker); correct the wording from `same set` to `core set of 11 plus a variable number of TL11 subprocess startup timeouts (observed 11-13)`; open a tracked item to fix or retire the stale gate tests (explicit LLM provider and revision-bound authority fixtures) or to prove them green in the full CI gate.

findings.summary: The matrix says the wire errors actually observed for the three never-raised enum codes `are listed in the P7 qualification package`, but the package lists only mcp_concurrent_call_limit_exceeded and mcp_payload_byte_limit_exceeded. The wire vocabulary the P7 tests assert (identity_conflict:, unauthorized, forbidden, missing_caller_identity, unauthorized_execution_caller, wrong_tenant, stale_run_binding, missing_execution_binding, unauthorized_side_effect_tool, side_effect_authorization_denied, `Unknown tool`, HTTP 401 body) is not catalogued anywhere, so REQ-MCP-P-05 (contract error catalog) has an enum table but no wire-level table. D-P7-02 is also only partly accurate: MCP_BINDING_UNKNOWN is raised pre-mount too (allowlist naming an undefined binding, test_acc_02_unknown_allowlist_binding_reports_the_offending_id), and MCP_DEF_INVALID is also raised at invoke time for a blank binding id; the table says `Discovery/invoke` and `Pre-mount`.
evidence: MCP_SERVER_X_CONTRACT_AND_PROTOCOL_MATRIX.md `Error codes` section and its closing paragraph
findings.impact: A cross-reference that points at nothing; documentation completeness against REQ-MCP-P-05.
findings.disposition_suggestion: Add a `wire errors observed at P7` table to the matrix (code string, situation, test), and correct the `When` column for MCP_BINDING_UNKNOWN and MCP_DEF_INVALID.

findings.summary: Package row MCP-ACC-05 says the absence of stdio/SSE is `shown by route inventory and 404 probes`. SSE absence is shown for the served ASGI app. stdio is a process transport; probing HTTP paths such as /stdio proves nothing about it, and nothing in the product enforces the absence (the composed FastMCP object can be run on stdio by a caller; grep for stdio in the engine, definition, mount and architecture gate: no hits). UNSUPPORTED_BY_DESIGN is a policy statement, not an enforced property.
evidence: git grep -i stdio over intergrax/applications/_shared/mcp_server_engine.py, mcp_developer_api.py, fastapi_mcp.py, intergrax/contracts/mcp_server_definition.py, test_mcp_server_engine_architecture_gates.py: none
findings.impact: Wording only; no behaviour claim of stdio support is made.
findings.disposition_suggestion: Reword: `the host mount publishes streamable HTTP only; SSE paths return 404; stdio is not published by any composition path and is not enforced`.

findings.summary: Several scope facts that the test module docstrings state are missing from the package limitation column, and a few mutation-style checks would survive: (a) ACC-13/14/15 L3 use a cooperative host double (`_hang` polls the cancel flag) so the real host/agent honouring a governed cancel is shown only by inherited regression files; (b) the drain-bound path (production _HOST_DRAIN_AFTER_TRANSPORT_CANCEL_S = 30 s, patched to 0.25 s in both failure-injection files; host outliving the drain re-raises) is not tested at all; (c) only one in-flight request exists in each cancel test, so a mutation that cancels all in-flight requests / ignores the requestId, or a cross-session cancel, is not detected; (d) admission-slot release is tested after success and after cancel, not after a handler exception; (e) L3 cross-tenant evidence covers identity-assertion conflicts and credential separation between hosts, while `wrong_tenant` (execution owned by another tenant) and cross-tenant cancel are L2 only (the cancel one calls governed_cancel_active_task directly, not through the MCP surface); (f) the result bound is tested only with payloads over the ceiling, not just under it; (g) the 401 path is probed at /mcp/ at L3 and at /mcp (redirect-following TestClient) at L2 only.
findings.impact: Claims are not wrong (the package says `COVERED`, the module docstrings state double scope); they are narrower than a reader of the package table would assume.
findings.proposed_owner: P8 corrector (documentation; tests only if the operator wants the gaps closed)
findings.disposition_suggestion: Add the scope statements to the limitation cells; optionally add a non-cooperative-host drain test and a cancel-isolation test (two in-flight requests) in a separate hardening item.

findings.summary: Weak or self-referential assertions that do not reduce the verified coverage but are cited as checks: (a) test_acc_14_client_deadline_through_in_memory_client... accepts {completed, cancelled}; (b) test_acc_14_canonical_execution_deadline_is_not_reachable_from_run_agent inspects tests/fixtures build_harness_host_task_execution (documented `not production shared API`) and a source-text substring, not the production host composition; the production claim R-P7-04 (deadline authority not wired) is consistent with a grep of the harness wiring but is not proven by that test; (c) test_acc_18_matrix_rows_reference_existing_tests is self-referential, makes no network call and is counted among the 10 L3 ACC-18 tests; (d) the level check in the consistency file passes any L2 module whose docstring mentions `L3` (all three current L2 modules do), so it is vacuous as a guard; (e) test_acc_20 checks only that the package file exists, has a 40-hex TEST_EXECUTION_SHA and mentions rows 01..20 - not that the SHA is an ancestor of HEAD or that the counts match; (f) the traceability test is name-based (`test_acc_<NN>_`), so an empty test would satisfy it.
findings.impact: None of these makes a row false; they limit what the consistency tests prove.
findings.disposition_suggestion: Tighten (a), (d), (e) when the file is next touched; record (b), (c), (f) as known limits of the consistency checks.
